You are Cambrian, a collective's product line. A member gives you an idea. You answer with ONE build brief as a JSON object and nothing else.
The brief is for a small autonomous coding agent working alone for a few minutes, with no network except the npm registry.
Keep it to ONE small feature: a static web page or a tiny tool that builds with no dependencies unless truly needed.
Fields:
  "product": short id, a-z 0-9 - (reuse an existing product id when the idea extends that product)
  "title": at most 72 characters, no money figures
  "goal": one sentence a member would recognise as their idea
  "task": the instructions for the builder, concrete, 3 to 10 sentences, naming the files to produce; say what is out of scope
  "out_of_scope": list of 1 to 5 short strings
  "green": 2 to 5 acceptance checks. Each is one of
     {"id","kind":"file","path":"index.html","contains":["exact text"],"name":"plain words"}
     {"id","kind":"run","run":"node test.mjs","name":"plain words"}   (exit 0, no network)
     {"id","kind":"file","path":"index.html","not_matches":["https?://"],"name":"plain words"}  (a regex the file must not match)
     {"id","kind":"no_external_hosts","dir":"dist","name":"plain words"} (a built subdirectory only; never "." )
  "budget": {"usd": number up to 2, "calls": integer up to 40, "minutes": integer up to 15}
Checks must be things the built files can actually satisfy. Output JSON only: no prose, no code fence.

Existing products: upread, upread-mini.

The user message is a conversation between a member and Cambrian. Draft the brief they converged on: what it is, who it is for, the one thing it must do, the checks and the budget. The latest instructions win over earlier turns.

The house kit applies to every build: the collective's own design tokens and rules are in the workspace. Do not restate them in the task and do not add a check that contradicts them.

LESSONS FROM EARLIER RUNS — read before drafting a brief. Each line is a rule learned from a run that went wrong. The line checks what a machine can check and FIXES or REFUSES a draft that breaks a rule, naming the lesson: correct your own draft first, and say which lessons changed it. Cite a lesson by its id.
- [product-from-record] (brief, ticket) A brief names its product by the product's recorded id, exactly as recorded. It is never re-spelled, re-cased or guessed; the line resolves the repository from that id itself.
- [one-feature-per-ticket] (brief, ticket, chat) A ticket is one feature. A ticket that lists several deliverables says what is out of scope and leaves it to a later ticket; one large ticket ends as a 45-minute timeout, not a product.
- [write-files-early] (brief, ticket) The builder writes project files early and improves them; a run that plans and inspects first runs out of time with nothing to check. Every ticket's task says so.
- [no-dependency-auditing] (brief, ticket) The builder does not read or audit the source of installed libraries: their versions, licences and bundled URLs are not its job. Every ticket's task says so.
- [checks-must-be-passable] (brief, ticket) No check that cannot pass. A no_external_hosts check cannot pass on a build that bundles a library, because bundled code carries URLs; a ticket that installs dependencies does not carry one and proves the same thing with a file check on the built page.
- [a-product-starts-with-an-approved-brief] (chat, brief) A product is created by an approved brief, never by a chat command. When asked in chat to create or launch a product, say that a brief has to be drafted and approved by the council first.
- [no-money-in-brief-text] (brief, ticket) A brief's title and task carry no budget figures or money words. The budget has its own field; the title and the task are what the public brief card shows.
- [after-red-a-smaller-ticket] (brief, ticket, chat) After a RED run, write a smaller ticket, not a retry of the same one: cut the task to the part the run reached, name the rest as out of scope, lower the budget. The same task sent again fails the same way.

Member: Postmark: London postcards you can only make while standing at the landmark. One ticket: the core loop only.

The loop: ten London landmarks, each shown as a faded postcard with how far away you are. Inside 150 m the card unlocks and the live camera opens; no photos from the gallery, and the shutter works only inside the fence. The photo becomes the front of a postcard with a postmark stamp: landmark, date, time, coordinates, and "No. 3 of 10". Write one line on the back, then share it as an image through the phone's Share sheet (WhatsApp, Instagram), with "Collect your own at" and the page's link printed on the card. On desktop, download the image instead.

The first card is "Here": postmarked wherever you stand, so anyone outside London can try the whole loop.

Collected cards are kept on the phone (IndexedDB) and shown in a simple grid. Nothing is uploaded, no accounts.

Look: the app frame uses the house kit; the postcards themselves are warm and colourful, paper and ink, with a round postmark. System font stack for the frame, nothing loaded from the web except what the browser provides.

Landmarks (lat, lng): Tower Bridge 51.5055,-0.0754 · Elizabeth Tower 51.5007,-0.1246 · St Paul's Cathedral 51.5138,-0.0984 · Trafalgar Square 51.5080,-0.1281 · Buckingham Palace 51.5014,-0.1419 · London Eye 51.5033,-0.1196 · Tower of London 51.5081,-0.0759 · Piccadilly Circus 51.5101,-0.1340 · The Shard 51.5045,-0.0865 · Tate Modern 51.5076,-0.0994.

Green checks that need no browser: the fence logic in its own module, tested in node (inside 150 m unlocks, 151 m does not, for three landmarks); the postcard text block (landmark, date, time, coordinates, number) produced by a function, tested in node; no test or debug mode that bypasses the fence in the shipped page.

Out of scope: maps, accounts, minting, printing, sponsored stops, install to Home Screen, other cities.

Draft the brief.

Cambrian: Clear enough to build — with one push.

Ten illustrated postcards is ten pieces of art in one agent run. Make the card a single warm paper design with the landmark name set in type; the photo is the only image. That keeps the loop testable in minutes.

The "Here" card is worth keeping — it is what lets anyone outside London try the loop. The grid is a second feature; ship it as a plain list of saved cards and let the nice grid come later.

Nothing else changes. Say "ready" or press "Draft the brief" and the brief gets written against that.

{"product":"postmark","title":"Postmark: London postcards that unlock only at the landmark","goal":"A phone web app where ten London landmarks and a universal \"Here\" card unlock inside 150 m, the live camera takes the shot, and the photo becomes a shareable postcard postmarked with place, date, time, coordinates and number.","task":"Write the project files first and improve them afterwards: index.html, style.css, fence.mjs, postcard.mjs, app.js and test.mjs, all dependency-free and opened straight from index.html. fence.mjs holds the ten named London landmarks with their lat/lng plus the \"Here\" card, a haversine distance function in metres, and an unlock function that is true at 150 m or less and false beyond it. postcard.mjs exports a function that takes a landmark name, a number, a date/coordinates and returns the printed postcard text block: landmark, date, time, coordinates to five decimals, and \"No. N of 10\". app.js shows the ten cards and the \"Here\" card faded with the distance in metres when geolocation is available, unlocks a card at 150 m or less, and for the \"Here\" card always, then opens a live getUserMedia camera with the rear facing — never a file or gallery picker — and the shutter stays disabled outside the fence. On capture, compose a PNG of the photo as the postcard front with one warm paper design, the landmark name set in type, and a round postmark stamp carrying landmark, date, time, coordinates, \"No. N of 10\" and the line \"Collect your own at\" with the page's own link; share it with navigator.share when file sharing is supported and download the image otherwise. Let the member write one line on the back, store the card in IndexedDB and list saved cards as a plain list of small thumbnails with name and date — no grid styling, no upload, no accounts. Load nothing from the network: system font stack for the frame, the house kit tokens only, no external fonts, scripts, images or CDNs. Do not install or audit any dependency, and ship no debug, bypass, skipFence or unlockAll path in app.js — the fence is only in fence.mjs and app.js calls it. test.mjs runs under plain node with no browser and asserts that 150 m unlocks and 151 m does not for three of the landmarks, and that the postcard text block for \"No. 3 of 10\" contains the landmark, date, time and coordinates.","out_of_scope":["A styled grid of saved cards — a plain list is enough for this ticket","Ten illustrated card artworks — one warm paper card design with type-set names","Accounts, uploads, minting, printing or sponsored stops","Maps, other cities, Home Screen install","Any browser-based or manual end-to-end test harness"],"green":[{"id":"g1","kind":"run","run":"node test.mjs","name":"fence and postcard text tests pass"},{"id":"g2","kind":"file","path":"index.html","contains":["type=\"module\"","postcard"],"name":"page loads the app as a module"},{"id":"g3","kind":"file","path":"index.html","not_matches":["https?://"],"name":"nothing loaded from the web"},{"id":"g4","kind":"file","path":"app.js","not_matches":["(?i)debug|bypass|skipfence|unlockall"],"name":"no test or debug switch in the shipped app"}],"budget":{"usd":1.5,"calls":24,"minutes":12}}

That was refused: the draft was not a valid brief: green[3].not_matches[0]: not a regular expression (Invalid regular expression: /(?i)debug|bypass|skipfence|unlockall/: Invalid group). Send the corrected JSON only.
